intro_lines: This game remembers the days you work. Finish a day and it goes on your profile, in a file on this computer only.
If you skip several days, your fictional boss writes you an increasingly dramatic letter. It costs a little in-game reputation and starting cash. Nothing real, ever.
You get 3 leave days per month, and you can request leave in advance from the title screen. You can switch the attendance letters off in Settings at any time.
text.intro_hint: No account, no network, no notifications. Your profile can be reset in Settings.
text.leave_hint: Next time, request leave on the title screen.
text.welcome_back: Welcome back bonus: +$%d on your starting wallet.
text.penalty_fine: Fine: -$%d from your next starting wallet
text.rehired_note: History kept. You restart as an Intern.

reminder.subject: Where were you?
lines: Your chair is feeling lonely. It asked me to ask you where you are.
I watered your desk plant. It says thanks and also that you are late.
The coffee machine asked about you. I said you were doing something important.
Nobody touched your stapler. It has been standing guard since yesterday.
Quick note: the office cat sat on your keyboard all morning. No data was harmed.
No pressure! Just a friendly knock on your virtual door.

warning.subject: Verbal warning (very verbal)
lines: I covered your desk plant again. It says it is not my coworker, it is your responsibility.
Ms. Hanh asked where you were. I said you were in a meeting with a very tall spreadsheet.
This is a gentle verbal warning. It is mostly my voice, and I am not very scary.
Your inbox is building a small mountain. It has named the peak after you.
The team lunch ordered your usual and had to eat it for you. It was a sacrifice.
Come back soon, or I will have to start answering your emails in your style.

fine.subject: Notice of small fine
lines: You have been absent for several days. A fine has been deducted. The coffee machine misses you more than the bank does.
HR has reviewed your attendance and found it creatively absent.
Please note that the fine is small, fictional and tax-free in all known universes.
Your name tag has started gathering dust. We dusted it. That cost money. Hence the fine.
Attendance is like a houseplant: skip it long enough and it files a complaint.
This letter was printed on very serious paper. The paper is a bit embarrassed about it.

formal.subject: Official warning
lines: Official warning. Your market forecast this week was 'I do not know' by not submitting. Bold choice.
I have seen better attendance from the office ghost, and we do not have an office ghost.
Your rank is at risk. Your desk is at risk. The sandwich in your drawer is definitely at risk.
I am not angry. I am disappointed, and also slightly angry, and mostly hungry.
Please report to your desk. Bring a forecast, a valid reason, or a funny hat.
This warning will be filed in the cabinet marked 'Dramatic Things'.

termination.subject: Termination notice (draft)
lines: Dear employee, this is a termination notice. Unless you have a valid reason, like a cat on the keyboard. Cat on keyboard counts.
We have prepared a farewell cake. It is already being eaten. Hurry back.
Your badge will stop opening doors at the end of the week. The doors are sad about it.
Per policy section 12, paragraph 'Please Come Back', this letter is mandatory and very dramatic.
Your colleagues have started telling stories about you in the past tense. Do something about it.
This is the point where a sad violin plays. We hired one. It is also an intern.

rehire.subject: You have been rehired
lines: Good news: we lost your termination paperwork and found your resume. You are rehired, as an Intern.
Your history is kept in a golden folder. Your title is kept in a smaller, less golden folder.
Welcome back! Khoi says you owe him a coffee for the cover story.
The Intern badge has your photo on it. We used the one where you look mysterious.
Everyone starts somewhere, and you start again here. The plant forgives you.
A fresh desk, a fresh mug and a fresh start. The old mug has retired to the shelf.

leave_reasons.text: A cat sat on my keyboard
Bus driven by a confident pigeon
